title: Soft limits, mid-cycle proration and metering edge cases for pricing/entitlements
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Background: Customers expect predictable billing when changing plans mid-cycle and when hitting soft (notify) vs hard (block) limits. This ticket defines requirements and acceptance criteria for: 1) soft-limit behavior with configurable grace windows, 2) proration and credit handling for mid-cycle plan upgrades/downgrades, 3) interaction between Dedicated reserved capacity and metered hosted usage, 4) per-route burst allowances (token buckets) and how they map to invoice line items, and 5) reconciliation / retroactive adjustments for invoice corrections. Goal: produce clear product requirements and acceptance tests so engineering and billing can implement deterministic, auditable behavior with minimal support overhead.
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: Soft-limit notifications: System must emit a 'soft_limit_warning' event when usage >= 85% of quota and a follow-up 'soft_limit_expiring' when usage continues for configurable grace window. Events must be visible in the Console activity feed and be queryable via the billing API for the org id and time range.

AC-2: Soft-limit grace window enforcement: For plans configured with a soft-limit grace window (0-7 days), additional usage during the window is allowed and billed at the customer’s current plan rate. At the end of the window, if usage > quota, behavior depends on the plan enforcement mode: 'auto-upgrade' (create overage invoice and optionally upgrade), 'soft-throttle' (apply rate-limiting hint), or 'block' (reject calls). The mode must be a plan attribute and honored by the runtime.

AC-3: Mid-cycle upgrade proration: Upgrades during a billing cycle must create a pro-rated credit for remaining days on the old plan and charge pro-rated amount for the new plan. The invoice must contain separate line items labeled 'prorated credit - old_plan' and 'prorated charge - new_plan' and the net must be reflected on the same billing period invoice.

AC-4: Mid-cycle downgrade handling: Downgrades must schedule entitlement changes to take effect at the next billing cycle by default, with an explicit 'apply immediately with credit' toggle for Finance-approved customers. When apply immediately is chosen, create a prorated negative balance or credit and ensure quota enforcement aligns with the new plan immediately.

AC-5: Reserved capacity interplay: Customers on Dedicated (reserved) plans who consume host-metered endpoints must not be double-billed. If reserved capacity covers tokens/throughput in a window, hosted-metered usage above reserved capacity should be billed as overage to the org's meter with tags referencing the reserved pool id. Billing must include the reserved commitment line item and separate overage lines if applicable.

AC-6: Per-route burst tokens: Route-level burst allowances (e.g., 1M burst tokens per 24h) are deducted from the org’s burst pool. Invoicing must surface burst consumption as a distinct usage SKU 'burst-tokens' with path metadata. Test: create traffic spike on route /embed and verify invoice line item surfaces 'burst-tokens' and corresponding cost.

AC-7: Meter reconciliation and retroactive adjustments: Finance must be able to create manual adjustments with an audit reason. Any retroactive adjustments older than 60 days must require manager approval. The system must surface an 'adjustment' line in invoices and link to the internal adjustment id in the console and billing API.

AC-8: Deleted/paused org edge-case: If an org is paused mid-cycle, usage during pause must be rejected and flagged; no metered charges should be created. If usage is retroactively found for a paused period, billing should create a support ticket tag and hold charges pending investigation; automated billing must not create an invoice for that usage without manual clearance.

AC-9: End-to-end test coverage: Create automated tests that simulate: (a) upgrade then heavy usage in grace window, (b) downgrade with immediate apply, (c) reserved capacity saturation and host-meter overage, (d) route burst surge generating burst-tokens invoice line. Tests must assert invoice line item labels, proration amounts, and Console visibility.

AC-10: Observability and customer-facing explanations: Console must show a timeline view for the billing period indicating quota thresholds crossed, grace windows, plan change timestamps, and exact proration math (rates, days remaining, credits). Explanations must be human-readable and include a 'view raw calculation' link that returns the underlying numeric values via the billing API.

AC-11: Backwards-compatible behavior: Default behavior for existing plans without explicit soft-limit configs must remain unchanged. Any change that affects in-flight orgs requires 14 days' notice and an automatic migration path preserving prior behavior until customer opt-in.
notes: Decision log 2025-02-10: Use 85% threshold as default soft-warning; product can change via plan template.
Trade-off: Allowing immediate downgrades with apply-immediately creates complexity for quota enforcement on shared reserved pools; recommended gating via Finance approval to reduce errors.
Implementation note: Billing team prefers explicit invoice line SKUs for proration and burst tokens to simplify downstream accounting; coordinate with Finance for SKU taxonomy.
Ops constraint: Retroactive adjustments >60 days require manager approval; implement approval workflow in Finance UI.
UX ask: Console timeline mockups required — linked design feedback below.
